messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Canary alert: service=inference-runtime canary=wave-7 region=us-west-2 metric=5xx_rate threshold=4.2% current=6.8% probe_failures=3/5 — paging oncall

alex.k: Ack, I'm on it. Seeing elevated 502/504s from the canary hosts.

morgan: @alex.k any recent rollouts or flag flips?

alex.k: Rolling out feature flag 'fastpath-v2' to 20% 15m ago. Canary subset pinned to the new path.

sasha: Oncall runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/canary-failures — check healthcheck logs and probe counts first.

alex.k: Pulling logs now. Quick tail: ```kubectl -n inference logs canary-pod-3 -c runtime | grep -E "5..|probe failed" -n | tail -n 50```

alex.k: Logs show a burst of connection resets and repeated backend 502 from runtime-ffi. Error: "kv-cache-miss-exception" appears a few times.

morgan: Huh, kv cache miss? Could be a kernel-level regression from the last runtime patch. Any model/quant changes?

alex.k: No model changes. Only fastpath-v2 routing and a small runtime shadow patch rolled earlier this morning (id: rtm-2024-06-15-ix).

remy: I'm looking at infra metrics: traffic to canary hosts is nominal, CPU/GPU fine, but p95 latency on health probes jumps right before 5xx spike. See dashboard: https://metrics.redwood/canary-wave7/2024-06-15

sasha: Given probe failures + 5xx, we should abort rollout for safety. Abort criteria: >5% 5xx for 5m OR >2 probe failures in 10m. We're past that. Recommend kill-switch.

alex.k: Agreed. Flipping flag to abort rollout — executing: ```curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTL_TOKEN" https://internal.flags.redwood/fastpath-v2/abort -d '{"reason":"canary 5xx spike"}'```

incident-bot: Flag change recorded by alex.k at 2024-06-15T13:12:34Z — fastpath-v2 -> abort.

morgan: :thumbsup: Flag flip acknowledged. Confirming traffic shift back to baseline model variants.

remy: Initiating automatic fallback: routing policy switched to stable pool (stable-variants) across us-west-2. Watching reroute metrics.

alex.k: Rolling back the runtime shadow patch as a precaution: ```ci-deploy rollback rtm-2024-06-15-ix --env=canary --reason="post-rollout 5xx"```

sasha: Please add the rollback ID to the incident notes.

alex.k: Rollback started — logs show pods terminating and new ones with previous image coming up. Pod readiness looks normal in 30s.

remy: 5xx rate dropping — current 5xx 1.1% across canary after traffic shift and rollback. Health probes recovering.

morgan: Good. Any customer-facing impact? Any reports?

alex.k: No active user tickets yet. Synthetic user tests saw failures during the spike (5 automated checks failed). I'll open a customer-impact check: contacting priority customers for the last hour of traffic.

sasha: Create an incident doc stub: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2024-06215-canary-wave7 — include timeline, flags, rollback id, metrics links. I'll own the postmortem.

alex.k: Done. Doc created and linked. Added initial timeline and commands executed.

remy: Handing off monitoring to oncall-next for the 2h stabilization window. @oncall-next please keep an eye on p95 probe latency and 5xx rate, escalate if 5xx >2% for more than 10m.

oncall-next: Ack, taking over. I'm stepping in now.

morgan: Quick note: we'll keep canary set at 0 traffic until next safe rollout window. Disable auto-rollouts for 24h.

alex.k: Auto-rollouts disabled in pipeline: ```ci-config set auto_rollout=false --scope=canary-wave-7```

sasha: Postmortem action items (initial): 1) Reproduce kv-cache-miss locally with current runtime patch. 2) Add canary probe rate limiting to reduce noise. 3) Improve abort criteria to include p95 probe latency.

remy: Also add a smoke test for fastpath routing under high prefix-cache churn.

alex.k: Agree. Will triage with runtime-team and slot a deep-dive tomorrow.

oncall-next: Monitoring for next 2h. Will update this thread with any regressions.

morgan: Thanks team. If stable in 2h, we'll close incident and move notes to postmortem. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2024-06215 created and assigned to sasha. Severity set to P2 due to transient canary-only impact.

oncall-next: 1740000200 — p95 probe latency back to normal, 5xx steady ~0.9%. No customer reports. Marking as stabilizing.

alex.k: Thanks everyone — handing off completely. Follow-ups via the incident doc.

oncall-next: 1740000300 — will close the monitoring window. Leaving final notes in the doc. :raised_hands:
